notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no Isaiah 6 notes for you yet.

My first attempt to open the source pages (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, Precept Austin, and Wesley's Notes) was refused. The system said I had no web tool calls left for this turn, and a second try was refused the same way. No page loaded, and my other tools can't reach the internet.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for every point. So I haven't written notes from memory, because they wouldn't come from sources I'd read and I couldn't give you real links.

If you ask again in a new turn, when the web tools should be available again, I'll work through the chapter verse by verse in the order you set:

1. **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word, BibleHub/StudyLight (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary) and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
   - Ligonier, Monergism and TGC (Reformed)
   - Spurgeon, Desiring God and GTY (Baptist)
   - Wesley's Notes and Seedbed (Methodist)
   - 1517 and LCMS (Lutheran)
   - Pneuma Review and Sam Storms (Pentecostal)

   I'd focus on the verses most likely to divide them, such as the hardening in vv. 9–10 and the "Us" in v. 8.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship; New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, for example how they understand the "Holy, holy, holy" in v. 3 and the coal from the altar in vv. 6–7. I'd add popular modern teaching only if these sites discuss it.

Each point would have its URL, and I'd leave out anything I can't find.
